### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-push`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-push/README.md`, `packages/services/service-push/package.json`, `packages/services/service-push/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**43** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-push/README.md`, `packages/services/service-push/package.json`, `packages/services/service-push/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4a6cbf319aa7b2b53d0bfcec08d3851cbf5ef3a` — the merge of head `d14d749e6b978c11f1d959ba985a21fd864d776e` into base `40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4a6cbf319aa7b2b53d0bfcec08d3851cbf5ef3a && git checkout d4a6cbf319aa7b2b53d0bfcec08d3851cbf5ef3a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11 d14d749e6b978c11f1d959ba985a21fd864d776e && git checkout -B drift-repro 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11 && git merge --no-ff d14d749e6b978c11f1d959ba985a21fd864d776e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40a9265ff3c8c3e96b1e2c13ea5edd1fb32e6d11` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1b82707de37511f76495017893bc60ecf63733f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/cloud-binding-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts + packages/services/service-push/src/transports/relay.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/push-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/capability-arg.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-push/vitest.config.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/transports/relay.test.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/push-plugin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-binding.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-binding.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-url.ts, packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/core/src/cloud-managed.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/push-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/system/core-services.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-email-sms.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, .changeset/29920-push-relay-cloud-binding.md, content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, docs/adr/0012-notification-platform.md, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs

Inputs: card #29920 (body and all 14 comments, rulings Q1 A, Q2 A, Q3 A at 6670221824, Q4 C at 6670237128 with correction 6670407970, dev report 6673285338), PR #30749 body and file list (37 files, identical to the local net diff against merge-base 4bf9a2d7), the net diff, and the check-runs on this head. Readings are against objectstack-ai/objectstack at `1b82707d` unless a base reading is named.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `PushRelayPayloadSchema.data` (api/push-relay.zod.ts): at base a `PushDeliveryDataSchema` object that STRIPS an undeclared key; at head `PushRelayPayloadDataSchema`, a `strictObject` over `PushDeliveryDataSchema.shape` that REFUSES one, with the ID-only guidance for `title`, `body`, `subtitle`, `message`, `content`. Narrowing. Right: carried item 1 (6606506582), and ADR-0012 §6.1 refuses those five by name; a stripped key read as carried was the hole. One source of the member list (the shape is reused, not transcribed), so no drift probe is owed.
2. `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.retryable`: at base inherited `z.boolean().default(false)` from `EnhancedApiErrorSchema`; at head `z.literal(true).default(true)`. Input accept set shrinks from true/false/absent to true/absent; the post-parse default flips from false to true. Narrowing. Right: carried item 2; a 429 rate limit is by definition retryable and a relay answering `retryable: false` on it was a lie the consumer would have obeyed. `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` keeps the inherited `false` default. Right.
3. `[PLANNED — not yet served]` removed from the seven relay object schemas' describes and from `PushRelayTransportConfigSchema`'s describe, plus the docblocks; `PushServiceConfigSchema` and the stack `push` key describes rewritten. Documentation-only on the public surface; no accept-set change. Right: ADR-0049 says a marker states a fact, and the sender ships in this PR; `push-relay.test.ts` and `push-config.test.ts` pin the absence.
4. `text` describe: "in the device locale" becomes "in the recipient's language". Right: ruling Q4 C, and that describe was named in the ruling as the spec half.
5. `PushServiceConfigSchema`, `PushRelayTransportConfigSchema`, the stack `push` key: the accept set is unchanged (relay with optional `endpoint`; direct with vendor blocks; inline secrets refused). Right: the ask was to serve what the schema already accepts, not to reshape it.
6. `ICloudBindingService` (new, `contracts/cloud-binding-service.ts`, exported through `contracts/index.ts`): `credential()`, `bound()`, `controlPlaneUrl()`. Additive; api-surface/contracts.json and export-origins/contracts.json regenerated with exactly that one row. Right: Q1 A as corrected (the `controlPlaneUrl()` member is the correction's).
7. `@objectstack/service-push` public surface: `PUSH_RELAY_NOT_SERVED_MESSAGE` leaves; `PUSH_RELAY_AIR_GAPPED_MESSAGE`, `RelayPushSender`, `relayTransport`, `PUSH_RELAY_PATH`, `CLOUD_BINDING_SERVICE`, `DEFAULT_PUSH_NOTICE`, `RELAY_NOT_BOUND`, `RELAY_ADDRESS_NOT_PUBLISHED`, `RELAY_BINDING_REFUSED`, `RelayPushSenderOptions` arrive; `IPushTransport.available?()` and `PushMessage.notice?` are new optional members; `IPushService.vendors()` now lists only AVAILABLE transports. The retirement is declared with its FROM → TO; the rest is additive. Right.
8. `@objectstack/core`: `CLOUD_DECLINED_SPELLINGS`, `isControlPlaneDeclinedSpelling`, `isControlPlaneDeclined` added beside `resolveControlPlaneApiKey`; `@objectstack/cloud-connection` re-exports `isControlPlaneDeclined` unchanged and `resolveCloudUrl` keeps its answers. Additive; one definition of the four spellings, read from two packages. Right (the cycle it avoids is real: cloud-connection depends on runtime).
9. `CloudConnectionPlugin` registers `cloud-binding` in `init()` and declares `providesServices` (ADR-0116); its own `kernel:ready` routes read `this.binding.credential()` instead of a local closure. Right: the one-owner half of Q1 A.
10. Metadata-protocol: none. Right. Nothing a metadata author writes gains, loses or changes meaning; the narrowings are on the server-to-relay request and the relay's error answer.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29920-push-relay-cloud-binding.md`: five packages (`service-push`, `cloud-connection`, `service-messaging`, `spec`, `core`) at `patch`, title `feat(service-push)!`, a BREAKING section, both declaration lines line-initial. The PR body carries the same two lines. Matches the diff: every package the diff moves is listed; nothing listed is untouched.
- Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — right, and BREAKING by the closed pair. The three narrowings it names (strict `data`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` retryable, the retired export) are the three the diff makes; the widening it also describes (relay configs now boot) is stated in prose and does not change the arm.
- `patch` on a BREAKING changeset: right by the Post-Task rule — the level follows the kind, `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` and keeps the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition.
- ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/service-push#PUSH_RELAY_NOT_SERVED_MESSAGE)` with a reason. Judged right (the reasoning is ③ item 1). Predicates as coded in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`: 1 retired-from-entry holds (exported from `service-push/src/index.ts` at base, absent at head); 2 no-metadata-surface holds (declared in no `*.zod.ts`, not under `spec/src/contracts/`, in no object definition at base); 3 from-operands-named holds (the one FROM line names exactly that operand; the two wire narrowings are instructions the detector does not read).
- The migration the BREAKING section owes is present: FROM `PUSH_RELAY_NOT_SERVED_MESSAGE` TO `PUSH_RELAY_AIR_GAPPED_MESSAGE` with the one-line fix, and one instruction each for the two wire narrowings.
- Changeset names the newly served relay transport, as the card's acceptance asks.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 1 — the ADR-0087 marker with the wire narrowings in prose (commit 2e35f600).** Accept A. Reasons: (a) the ledger is the data source of `objectstack migrate meta`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide, all of which describe STORED metadata; the relay wire is built per send by `RelayPushSender` and read once by the cloud relay, authored by nobody and persisted nowhere, so a `registered` entry would be a conversion with nothing to convert, projected into two machine-readable artifacts as a migration that does not exist (Route and surface ownership rule 4); (b) the changeset stock's `registered` narrowings of a spec `*.zod.ts` are all authorable metadata keys (validation, picklist binding, permission, field sortable, flow condition) — a different class; (c) the gate's purpose is that the question is answered in writing, and the marker's reason does that for the wire; (d) the category's three predicates hold as coded (② above). Alternative B is refused: it would also widen the surface into `packages/spec/src/migrations/` for an entry the ledger should not carry. No surface amendment needed.

**Open question 2 — two anchored source aliases in `service-push/vitest.config.ts`.** Accept. `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` carries no `service-push` row and is shrink-only, so the new VALUE imports of `@objectstack/spec/api` (relay.ts, relay.test.ts) and `@objectstack/core` (push-plugin.ts, capability-arg.ts) had to be aliased, not registered; the anchored regex array form is the shape the gate's own header prescribes against the `ENOTDIR` trap; the crossing into `core/src` feeds rule 5 only. The mechanical verdict is the `Lint · repo & tooling gates` check on this head, in progress at review time (the dev reports it green locally at `1b82707d`).

**Open question 3 — `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx` edited outside the claim's listed surface.** Accept. The `kernel/` tree is hand-written (Documentation Guardrails: every tree except `references/` and `releases/`), no page is added so no `meta.json` is owed, and the page documented an init refusal this PR removes: leaving it would advertise a refusal the runtime no longer makes (Prime Directive 10's corollary, inverted). Content read against the diff: the authentication, address, ID-only, unbound and air-gap paragraphs and the availability table row match `relay.ts`, `push-plugin.ts` and `push-channel.ts`. The seat records the surface widening on the card in one line; no further action.

**Other flags from the dev report, answered:**
- `CLOUD_BINDING_SERVICE` spelled in cloud-connection and service-push: a should-fix on the contract file (④ item 2), not noted-and-closed.
- `results.find(…) ?? results[0]`: not a finding — `PushRelayResponseSchema` promises one result per delivery in request order and the request carries one delivery, so index 0 IS the delivery's answer.
- `OS_CLOUD_URL` unset but the plugin option `controlPlaneUrl: 'off'`: accepted as noted. The ruling's text is `isControlPlaneDeclined()`, which reads the environment; under `objectstack serve` the option is `resolveCloudUrl()`'s own answer so the two cannot disagree; a hand-composed host hits a loud, per-send, non-retryable `relay_address_not_published`. The related seam the dev did not note is ④ item 2's second finding.
- ADR-0012 at head still says the relay is "not yet served" (status line, §4 table row, the §6 amendment note, §6.1's "what main serves") and names `PUSH_RELAY_NOT_SERVED_MESSAGE` by path. `docs/adr/**` is excluded by the claim and is Tier H. These are dated readings ("at this amendment", "at 6a4737ab"), not decisions this PR reverses, so Prime Directive 13 is not breached; the staleness goes to #30670 (ADR-0012 §6.1 docs card) or a sibling docs-only PR. Should-fix, routed, not blocking.
- Startup-registry-verdict rule: the `kernel:ready` warn in `PushServicePlugin.start()` reads the credential store (not a filling registry), after every `init()`, says the state can change, and records nothing; the per-send `ctx.getService('cloud-binding')` read is a read-only probe. Clear.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts** — holds. Against ADR-0012 §6.1: the five content keys are refused by name at both the payload and the data layer, `text` is the only visible line, and the docblock now names the producer (`RelayPushSender`), the parse before send and the cloud control plane as the receiver (cloud#3519). Against the first consumer `relay.ts`: the request is parsed with `PushRelayRequestSchema` before `fetch`, so a content key in `PushMessage.data` ends as `relay_payload_refused` with the issue path and nothing leaves the server (pinned); the 200 answer is read with `PushRelayResponseSchema`; 401 and 429 with `PushRelayErrorResponseSchema`, and the 429 arm reads `error.retryable` from the parsed union — `true` for `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` whether the relay sent it or not, `false` for `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (pinned both ways); a 429 whose body fails the parse falls to retryable, the safe direction. Break attempts: `.default(true)` on a literal inside a `discriminatedUnion('code', …)` is legal (the discriminator is `code`); `PushDeliveryDataSchema.shape` read inside a `lazySchema` factory resolves the proxy on first use; the non-exported `PushRelayPayloadDataSchema` leaves api-surface/api.json unchanged and the docs generator inlines it (push-relay.mdx regenerated). No finding.

**packages/spec/src/contracts/cloud-binding-service.ts** — holds against Q1 A as corrected: three members, read on every call, `''` when unbound, the credential rule stated once and matching `createCloudBinding` (`resolveControlPlaneApiKey(option) || store.read()?.runtimeToken || ''`), and the secret-handling line the consumer keeps (`relay.ts` puts the credential in `authorization` and in no error text or log line; pinned). Two should-fixes:
1. **should-fix** — the service NAME belongs beside the interface. Six sibling contracts export their name constant from the contract file (`EMBEDDER_SERVICE`, `KNOWLEDGE_SERVICE`, `OWNERSHIP_QUEUE_SERVICE`, `RLS_MEMBERSHIP_RESOLVER_SERVICE`, `SEED_SETTLEMENT_SERVICE`, `FILE_ATTACHMENT_SERVICE`); this PR spells `CLOUD_BINDING_SERVICE = 'cloud-binding'` in `cloud-connection/src/cloud-binding.ts` and again in `service-push/src/transports/relay.ts`, with no dependency between the two and no cross-package test holding them equal (push-plugin.test.ts sets the literal `'cloud-binding'`, which pins service-push's copy only). Export `CLOUD_BINDING_SERVICE` from the contract, import it in both, regenerate api-surface and export-origins.
2. **should-fix** — the docblock promises `controlPlaneUrl()` is `''` only when the deployment declared no control plane, but `createCloudBinding` answers `resolveCloudUrl(option)`, whose `??` treats an explicit empty option as "not declined" and returns the production default — while the plugin's own routes read the same option as `(cfg.controlPlaneUrl ?? env ?? '')` and treat `''` as "cloud unconfigured" (cloud-connection-plugin.ts, line 337 at head). Two readers of one option inside the one plugin the ruling made the owner, disagreeing on `''`. Unreachable under `objectstack serve` (`planMarketplaceWiring` composes the plugin only when `resolveCloudUrl()` is non-empty, and passes that value), so not a must-fix; a hand-composed `new CloudConnectionPlugin({ controlPlaneUrl: '' })` reaches it. Fix: the routes derive `cloudUrl` from `this.binding.controlPlaneUrl()` as they now do for the credential, with the binding reading `''` the way the routes do, or the docblock states what `''` answers.

**packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts** — holds: one `export *` line in the barrel's order, comment names the registrar and the reader. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts** — holds against Q2 A: the `push` key's docblock and describe now say absent reads as the relay, which sends once bound and is refused at boot only when `OS_CLOUD_URL` declares no control plane. That is exactly what `resolvePushCapabilityArg` does at head (`config.transport === 'relay' && isControlPlaneDeclined()`), and `stack-email-sms.test.ts` keeps authoring accepting both transports and the absence. No stale "relay sender ships" text remains under `content/docs/references/`. No finding.

**packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts** — holds against Q2 A and its first consumer `push-plugin.ts`: both transports served; the relay reads the binding on every send; an unbound server boots, lists no vendor (`PushService.vendors()` honours `available()`), the channel's existing `isAvailable` answers `transport_not_configured` (the closed reason set does not grow), one warn at `kernel:ready`; refused at boot only when declined, with the air-gap refusal naming both ways out. The relay block's shape (`endpoint` optional, no credential) is unchanged and `relay.ts` honours `endpoint` over the control-plane path. One should-fix beside it: **should-fix** — `packages/spec/src/system/push-config.test.ts` lines 204–207 still head the describe with "The relay is refused at boot until its sender ships (#29920), so its block keeps a marker that says so", and the test two lines below pins the opposite; rewrite the comment to the served reading.

No must-fix found. Check-runs on `1b82707d` at review time: no conclusion is red; completed `success`: Auto Label, Check PR Size, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Validate Package Dependencies, Dogfood Regression Gate (gate job), Plan Test Core shards, filter; `skipped` by paths filter: UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, 18.x upgrade harness, Schedule gate, Packed-tarball smoke; still `in_progress`: Test Core 1/8–8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, every `Lint ·` job (ESLint; repo and tooling gates; docs and code guards; CI, release and engine gates; PM dispatch-gates; the three scoped lanes) and every `Type Check ·` job (workspace; source gates; consumer gates; debt ledger). The required contexts therefore have no verdict yet; this record does not substitute for them, and the seat reads their conclusions before any landing step.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d14d749e6b978c11f1d959ba985a21fd864d776e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0012-notification-platform.md, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.test.ts + packages/services/service-push/src/transports/relay.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/push-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-binding.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/cloud-binding-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/push-channel.ts, scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs, scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs

Delta review: one commit on top of `1b82707d` (record 6673473934, PASS), `d14d749e` "docs(adr): ADR-0012 reads the hosted push relay as served", 2 files, 8 lines each way. Inputs: the delta diff (`git diff 1b82707d d14d749e`), card #29920 including the claim amendment 6673499048 (surface widened to the four ADR-0012 readings this PR makes false, gate-forced by `check:adr-symbol-anchors` red on `1b82707d`), the PR body and file list (38 files), and the 66 check-runs on this head. The earlier record's ① and ② stand unchanged for the 36 files this commit does not touch; the earlier should-fixes 3 and 4 are the ones this commit addresses.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set change: the commit touches a governed prose surface and a test's heading comment. No schema, export or test assertion moves. Right.
- The ADR-0012 Status line, the §4 `push` row's last cell, the §6 dead-token amendment note and the §6.1 "What `main` serves" bullet now read the relay as served; every other line of the ADR is byte-unchanged, the §6.1 privacy bullet's "in the device locale" half-sentence included (one occurrence before and after). Right: #30670 owns that wording, as ruled (6670237128 item 6).
- The four readings this commit replaces were the only ones in `docs/adr/**` that said the relay was unserved (the grep at head finds the four phrases only inside the quotations the amended passages carry). Right.
- `push-config.test.ts` lines 202–205: the heading comment now says both transports are served and the relay is refused at boot only on a deployment that declared no control plane, which is what the describe beneath it pins. Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6673473934: five packages at `patch`, `feat(service-push)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, the ADR-0087 `not-required (runtime-export-retired …)` marker with its three predicates holding. A docs/adr edit and a test comment publish nothing and move no declaration. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags
